solution: L'Hopital's rule would need nine differentiations of a nested tangent; use the series instead
solution_full: Near $0$, $N(x)$ is small, so $N(N(x))$ is defined. Differentiating $N(N(x))$ nine times is impractical, so the Maclaurin series of $\tan$ is used.

Write $\dfrac{N(N(x))}{x^{9}}=\dfrac{N(u)}{u^{3}}\cdot\dfrac{u^{3}}{x^{9}}$. The first factor tends to $-\dfrac{1}{3}$ (because $u\to0$) and the second to $-\dfrac{1}{27}$.
Hence the limit is $\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{27}\right)=\dfrac{1}{81}$. (Dropping one sign gives $-\dfrac{1}{81}$; treating $N(N(x))$ as $N(x)^{3}$ gives $-\dfrac{1}{27}$.)
originality_note: New: the map t -> t - tan t is applied twice; each application cubes the size and multiplies by -1/3, so the composite is of order x^9 with coefficient (-1/3)(-1/3)^3 (way 1, iteration). Closest known: lim (tan x - x)/x^3 and the JEE Main 2025 limit of (tan(tan x) - sin(sin x))/(tan x - sin x). Different because: the composition is of a function that vanishes to third order, so the orders multiply (3 x 3 = 9) instead of the cubic coefficients adding.
blueprint_concepts: Evaluation of limit involving trigonometric functions
Taylor / Maclaurin Series Expansion: Evaluating indeterminate limits where L'Hôpital fails or becomes cumbersome.

concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving trigonomet: lim (t - tan t)/t^3 = -1/3 is the trigonometric limit used at both stages.
concept_use.Evaluation of limit using expansion: The expansion tan t = t + t^3/3 + ... gives N(t) = -t^3/3 + O(t^5) and u^3 = -x^9/27 (1 + O(x^2)).
concept_use.Taylor / Maclaurin Series Expansion: Eva: The x^9 order of a nested tangent makes L'Hopital impractical (nine differentiations); the series of the composite settles it.
